repository_entries.description: Automatically label selected issue modules and maintain release labels on new and reused tracking issues.
Add published project release notes to the documentation site, including component changes and version-only bumps.
Validate synthetic KMS requests and document local HTTP contract coverage.
Add stateful DynamoDB Local acceptance for idempotency and parameter adapters.
Test affected modules during ordinary CI and require full module, runtime and DynamoDB Local regression before release publication.
Document the current Go 1.27 and JSON v2 contract in existing guides and examples.
Compare DynamoDB service acceptance response values independently of JSON object member order.
Add reproducible core-utility microbenchmarks and scoped allocation/output baselines.
Provide a complete minimal Lambda example and explicit documentation and acceptance version policy.
Define issue-driven v1 readiness gates and publish scoped historical AWS acceptance.
Prepare explicitly versioned unified release candidates with validated progression and ordinary publication gates.
Record reviewed v1 candidate preparation and publication acceptance gates separately from source acceptance.

Use opaque reflection identity tokens without explicit unsafe-pointer values during deep merging.

### powertools-lambda-go/eventhandler/http

#### Breaking changes

- Encode JSON bodies with v2 collection and field-omission defaults and reject ambiguous raw events. ([#111](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/111))

#### Fixes

- Respect Accept-Encoding quality values, wildcard overrides and identity preference when choosing compression. ([#79](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/79))
- Decode structured +json media types before request and response body validation. ([#80](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/80))
- Preserve 204, 205 and 304 statuses when buffered response bodies are empty. ([#81](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/81))
- Honor explicit proxy response encoding without double-encoding preencoded string bodies. ([#82](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/82))
- Preserve native binary buffers and typed byte/reader bodies across Lambda HTTP response adapters. ([#82](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/82))
- Preserve buffered cookie values including Expires commas and arbitrary v1/ALB repeated header arrays. ([#83](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/83))
- Keep supported header values during headers-only Streaming projection for every adapter. ([#83](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/83))
- Bound error-handler redispatch and honor cancellation between callbacks. ([#84](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/84))
- Normalize GET and HEAD request bodies across Lambda HTTP adapters without conversion failures. ([#85](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/85))

#### Documentation

- Document native Lambda routing, response ownership and a public route example. ([#104](https://github.com/rambow-cloud/powertools-lambda-go/pull/104))
